claims.text: Becoming self-aware by viewing one's own Facebook profile enhances self-esteem.
Updating one's profile during Facebook exposure leads to greater reported self-esteem.
Selective self-presentation in digital media influences impressions of the self.

evidence.description: The results revealed that, in contrast to previous work on OSA, becoming self-aware by viewing one's own Facebook profile enhances self-esteem rather than diminishes it.
Participants that updated their profiles and viewed their own profiles during the experiment also reported greater self-esteem, which lends additional support to the Hyperpersonal Model.
These findings suggest that selective self-presentation in digital media, which leads to intensified relationship formation, also influences impressions of the self.

methodologies.name: Controlled Facebook Exposure Experiment
methodologies.description: An experiment testing self-esteem outcomes after participants view or update their own Facebook profiles, contrasting Objective Self-Awareness theory and the Hyperpersonal Model.
